Treatment of Adverse Effects Acute poisoning due to the ingestion of arsenic compounds should be treated by immediate gastric lavage if the patient presents within 1 hour and has not already vomited. Activated charcoal has been used to reduce absorption but is unlikely to be of benefit unless a significant amount of arsenic has been ingest- ed. Intravenous replacement of fluids and electrolytes should be undertaken as necessary to correct dehydration and electrolyte imbalance; pressor agents may be required. Chelation therapy should start immediately the cause of arsenic poisoning is suspected. The therapy of choice for acute poison- ing is unithiol (p.1468) given intravenously in cases of gastroin- testinal toxicity. Dimercaprol (p.1444) given intramuscularly is the second choice therapy if unithiol is unavailable. Oral therapy with unithiol or succimer (p.1466) should be substituted when gastrointestinal disturbances are no longer a problem.
